span.label: The distractor-response binding paradigm itself - a prime-probe protocol for separating distractor-based response retrieval from distractor inhibition.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: How can distractor-based response retrieval and distractor inhibition be measured separately when studying how ignored stimuli influence human action control?
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Re-encountering a stimulus that was bound into an event file retrieves the whole stored episode, including the response executed with it, so an ignored distractor can drive the current response.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Retrieval runs in parallel with the algorithm computing the required response, so the longer the response takes, the more often retrieval finishes in time to influence it - which is why slower tasks show larger binding effects.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Inhibiting the same distractor twice in a row carries after-effects that facilitate the second inhibition, producing a benefit that is independent of whether the response repeats.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A stimulus and a response executed close together in time are stored as one episodic trace, so re-encountering the stimulus retrieves the whole episode including the response
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Because the distractor is bound into the same trace as the target and response, the distractor alone can trigger retrieval of the target's response
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Retrieval therefore helps when the response repeats and hurts when it changes, which is why the signature is an interaction rather than a main effect
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Inhibition predicts a benefit from distractor repetition that does not depend on response repetition, which is what makes the two mechanisms separable in one design
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Retrieval runs in parallel with computing the required response, so slower tasks give retrieval more time to finish and produce larger effects
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The factors that modulate the distractor-response binding effect are not yet fully specified.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paradigm has been validated in only one clinical sample (unpublished), so the trial numbers needed for individual-difference work are unknown.
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[4]
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The effect fails if the gap between prime response and probe onset is too long
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Grouping of target and distractor appears to be required, and the full set of modulating conditions is not yet known
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Only one clinical sample has been looked at, and that data is unpublished, so trial numbers for individual-difference work are unknown
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Error rates usually yield nothing, so the paradigm effectively rests on response times alone
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Trials repeating the target identity must be dropped from analysis to keep target-based bindings out, yet kept in the procedure to stop participants responding strategically
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paradigm is modality-independent: the same binding effect and the same response-time modulation appear in visual, auditory and tactile versions, which the paper reads as evidence that the mechanism is central rather than perceptual
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Repeating a distractor speeds responding when the same response must be repeated, because the distractor retrieves a compatible response.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Repeating a distractor slows responding when the response must change, because the distractor retrieves the now-incompatible response.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paradigm's central advantage is that response retrieval shows up as the response-by-distractor interaction while distractor inhibition shows up as the distractor main effect, so the two mechanisms can be read off separately from the same design.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Across 33 published experiments the binding effect grew larger as tasks got harder and mean response times got longer.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A single function describes how response time modulates the binding effect in visual, auditory and tactile experiments alike, implying a central rather than modality-specific mechanism.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The interval between the prime response and probe onset must be short: no binding effect appeared at an onset asynchrony of 1,500 msec.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Presenting target and distractor grouped together appears to be a precondition for the effect.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Error rates usually carry no significant effects because participants commit too few errors.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Shortening stimulus presentation to 300 msec, imposing an 800 msec response window, or varying the prime-probe gap between 150 and 350 msec all leave the result pattern intact.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Unpublished data from participants with autism spectrum disorder suggest the effect is obtainable in a clinical sample with the same number of trials.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
